process_observations.observation: The org's three findings so far (N3-F-02 Probability, N3-F-03 Name, N3-F-04 StageName) line up with a real, checkable Salesforce fact independent of this build: Name, StageName and CloseDate are the three standard fields the platform marks required at the field level (nillable=false) on Opportunity. That correspondence is what makes the CloseDate bet a reasoned inference rather than a guess, and it is exactly the kind of pattern-across-findings signal this build's Process Observations exist to surface.

The re-run checker output is unchanged for the third consecutive repair: one REVIEW (identical-layout merge candidate), one INFO (no Profile/PermissionSet in scope), exit 0. Three consecutive behavior-only edits applied identically to both files have not disturbed either finding, which is the expected result of edits that only ever add or flip a behavior value inside an already-scanned layoutItems entry.

This is the first repair in this sequence where an artefact edit is not fully backed by a deploy message against this build - CloseDate's Required behavior is inferred, not confirmed. The instruction that produced it is explicit and disclosed (deploy-order.md §6's UNVERIFIED (2026-09-18) marker, this envelope's confidence_rationale), which is the correct way to make a documented bet rather than a silent one, but it is still a departure from every prior fix in this step, each of which followed rather than anticipated an org message.

Run 4's three possible outcomes are all live: (a) it passes cleanly, silently confirming CloseDate was correctly anticipated; (b) it is silent on CloseDate specifically but names a fifth field, meaning CloseDate may or may not have been necessary and the bet is untested either way; (c) it reports CloseDate itself was wrong somehow (unlikely given the field-level-required fact, but not something a dry run against this specific layout/record-type/profile combination has actually exercised). deploy-order.md §6 names outcome (a) and asks for the marker to be resolved either way, but does not fully disambiguate (b) from a true confirmation. Worth a second look once run 4's actual report lands.

M1-S02 has now cycled built -> running three times for org-discovered repairs (run-1 fix via documented->running, run-2 fix via tested->failed->pending->running, this run via built->running directly since no tester ran between run-2's built and this instruction). All three are legal edges per standards/build-orchestration.md § 4 and each was named explicitly by the invocation rather than chosen by this agent, but a reader of plan.json's runs[] history should not assume a uniform recovery path across the three - the edge taken depended on which status the step happened to be in when each org finding arrived.
